Project Engineer – Civil Infrastructure Western Sydney (near Western Sydney Airport) | Immediate Start
 Join a major civil infrastructure project helping deliver critical works within one of Australia's fastest-growing development corridors.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 We are seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the delivery of a large-scale civil infrastructure project involving bulk earthworks, utilities, roads, drainage and associated subdivision works.
 Working closely with the Project Manager and site delivery team, you will play a key role in coordinating subcontractors, managing consultant and design interfaces, resolving technical queries and ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
 The role will involve significant coordination between site teams, subcontractors, design consultants and external stakeholders to ensure design documentation, approvals and construction activities remain aligned with the project programme.
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing contractor with a strong pipeline of work across Western Sydney.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Coordinate day-to-day project delivery activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Manage subcontractors, suppliers, consultants and design interfaces.
 - Coordinate with civil, structural, services and other design consultants to resolve technical and construction-related issues.
 - Manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design clarifications, ensuring timely responses from relevant consultants.
 - Support design management activities, including design reviews, documentation coordination, constructability assessments and design changes.
 - Monitor design deliverables, approvals and outstanding information to ensure construction activities remain on programme.
 - Prepare and manage RFIs, NCRs, ITPs, SWMS reviews and project documentation.
 - Monitor programme, productivity and project milestones.
 - Assist with procurement, scope packages and subcontractor management.
 - Track project costs, variations and progress claims.
 - Support quality assurance and compliance activities across site.
 - Liaise with client representatives, authorities and key project stakeholders.
 - Prepare regular project reporting and progress updates.
 - Drive efficient project outcomes through proactive problem solving and coordination.
 SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
 - Experience as a Project Engineer within civil infrastructure, subdivisions or earthworks projects.
 - Strong understanding of bulk earthworks, roads, drainage and utility installation.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering consultants and managing design-related issues during construction.
 - Ability to manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design documentation.
 - Experience reviewing construction drawings, identifying design discrepancies and coordinating practical solutions.
 - Strong subcontractor management, project documentation and stakeholder coordination skills.
 - Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple work fronts in a live construction environment.
 - Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 - Proficient with project management and reporting systems such as Procore, Laminar or similar.
 - Relevant Civil Engineering qualification.
 THE OPPORTUNITY
 - Major infrastructure project within the Western Sydney Airport growth corridor.
 - Long-term project pipeline and strong job security.
 - Exposure to large-scale civil infrastructure and subdivision works.
 - Broad involvement across engineering, design coordination and construction delivery.
 - High-performing and collaborative project team.
 - Genuine career progression opportunities.
 THE DETAILS
 - Full-time, site-based position.
 - Western Sydney location.
 - Competitive salary package based on experience.
 - Immediate start available.
 HOW TO APPLY
 Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.
You’ve built your technical skills. You’re ready to take on more responsibility, contribute your ideas and develop the confidence to lead.
Rain Consulting is looking for a Project Engineer or Scientist with 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience to join our Melbourne team.
We’re a specialist stormwater and surface water consultancy. We plan and design better water environments, investigate how water behaves and help clients turn complex information into decisions they can act on.
Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.
And behind each challenge, there are people who need help turning complex information into a clear way forward.
These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.
We want you to question assumptions and contribute ideas. If you see a better way to approach a problem, explain a result or manage water, there’s room to explore it with us.
As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.
We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences.

bullets: Fully funded degree plus paid study leave every semester.

Build your career through Council's Emerging Talent Program.
candidates.content_text:
A career with Bega Valley Shire Council offers the opportunity to engage in meaningful and diverse work that supports the vibrant communities of the south-east corner of NSW. Nestled between rolling hills and some of the state’s most stunning beaches, this region is home to a variety of people who enjoy both rural and coastal living.
As an AR Bluett Award winning Council, we are proud of our dedicated and talented team, whose efforts make our success possible.
With a workforce of over 350, we provide essential services to our communities, including libraries, customer service, finance, children’s services, engineering, project management, road maintenance, water management, environment, parks, gardens, and town centres.
We offer a range of employment benefits to support our staff, which may include:
 - Rostered days off
 - Flexible work arrangements
 - Salary packaging
 - Paid study leave (one paid study day per week during each university semester or trimester)
 - Council-funded course fees and approved study-related expenses
 The Opportunity
We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated individual to join Councils Emerging Talent Program and undertake an undergraduate qualification in Engineering (honours) or a related discipline while gaining practical experience and mentorship across Council's Infrastructure Directorate.
As an Engineer Cadet, you will combine academic studies with hands-on workplace experience across a range of areas including Works and Projects, Water and Sewer Services, Asset Management, Design and Technical Services. You will gain exposure to infrastructure planning, project delivery, asset management, engineering design and technical services while developing practical skills within a local government environment.
The role may also involve travel and participation in residential study blocks associated with your academic program.
As a participant in Council's Emerging Talent Program, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills through structured learning, on-the-job experience, mentoring and exposure to a broad range of professional disciplines, building a strong foundation for a successful career in local government and beyond.
Council will support your studies by providing one paid study day per week during each university semester or trimester, together with funding for approved course fees and study-related expenses.
Key responsibilities include:
 - Assist in the delivery of engineering services across a range of functions, including project management, asset management, engineering design, inspections and technical services.
 - Assist with the planning, delivery, monitoring and evaluation of engineering projects and programs that support Council's infrastructure network.
 - Develop practical skills in data analysis, technical investigations, reporting, surveying, site inspections and project documentation.
 - Contribute to the delivery of engineering services that comply with statutory requirements, relevant standards and Council policies and procedures.
 - Apply your university learning in a practical environment while developing the technical, analytical and professional skills required for a successful career in engineering.
 This role offers valuable exposure to a broad range of infrastructure services while developing practical skills and experience to support a future career in engineering.
To view the Position Description, please click here.
About You
We are seeking an individual who holds a Higher School Certificate (or equivalent) and is eligible to enrol in an Engineering (Honours) degree.
You will have the following skills and experience;
 - Demonstrated interest in engineering, infrastructure, science or related technical disciplines.
 - Good written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to liaise effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
 - Demonstrated experience using the Microsoft Office suite.
 - Analytical thinking and the ability to solve problems logically and systematically.
 - Willingness to learn and apply knowledge gained through academic studies in a practical workplace environment.
 - Ability to work collaboratively within a team while managing competing priorities and meeting deadlines.
 Benefits
This is a fixed term full-time position working 35 hours per week for a period of six (6) years.
The total remuneration package for this position commences at $57,401.34 gross per annum, comprising of:
 - $985.60 per week base salary
 - $118.27 per week superannuation (calculated at 12%)
 Additional benefits for this position include:
 - Rostered day off scheme (nine day fortnight)
 - Paid study leave, providing one paid study day per week during each university semester or trimester
 - Council-funded course fees and approved study-related expenses
 - Annual Award salary increases and performance reviews
 - Salary packaging program (SmartSalary)
 - Wellbeing Initiatives – Fitness Passport, Employee Assistance Program, Telus Health App, social club, health monitoring and annual flu vaccinations.
 For further information on this position, please contact Brenton Blair, Technical Services Coordinator on 02 6499 2229.
Applications close 11.59pm AEDT on 22 November 2026.
Applicants must have the right to work in Australia and address the advertised selection criteria demonstrating their suitability for the role.

 Aquirian Limited (ASX: AQN) is a leading provider of people, equipment and technology solutions to the mining and resources sector. Through our specialised businesses, including Maglok, we develop and deliver innovative products and services that help our clients operate more safely, efficiently and profitably.
 At Maglok, innovation drives everything we do. We design, manufacture and continuously improve products that solve real operational challenges faced by defence and mining companies across Australia.

 This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a dynamic defence and mining technology business that develops practical, innovative solutions for the defence, mining and resources industry. You'll play a key role in the design, development, testing and implementation of products and technologies that improve safety, productivity and operational performance for our clients.
 Reporting to the Operations Manager, this position will work closely with our workshop team to deliver design, drafting and engineering support across a range of standard and custom projects.
 You will be responsible for assisting the Operations Manager and workshop team with mechanical design and drafting, developing specialised tooling and workshop improvements, supporting product development initiatives, and contributing to automation projects that will shape the future of mining technology.
 This role also includes responsibility for managing the small workshop stores area, including stocktakes, inventory control and material management.

 You are an energetic, self-motivated and technically capable Mechanical Designer or Engineer who enjoys working in a practical environment.
 You will bring a strong foundation in mechanical design, excellent problem-solving abilities and a genuine desire to learn, innovate and contribute as part of a collaborative team.
 Essential Requirements
 - Degree or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
 - Experience in mechanical design and drafting.
 - Proficiency in Autodesk Inventor and AutoCAD.
 - Strong understanding of mechanical design principles and manufacturing processes.
 - Experience producing engineering drawings and technical documentation.

 - Ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities.

 - Commitment to safety, quality and continuous improvement.

 Desirable Experience

 - Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience.
 - Product development, prototyping and testing experience.
 - Workshop, fabrication or practical manufacturing experience.
 - Inventory management or workshop stores experience.
 Why Join Maglok?
 This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing Australian mining technology company and contribute to the development of innovative products used throughout the resources sector.
 We Offer
 ✅ Competitive salary package
 ✅ Supportive and collaborative environment
 ✅ Modern workshop facilities located in Lonsdale, SA
 ✅ Hands-on involvement from concept design through to implementation
 ✅ The opportunity to deliver real productivity gains and cost savings for mining clients
 Apply Now
 If you're looking for a role where you can apply your engineering expertise, drive innovation and make a genuine impact on the future of mining technology, we would love to hear from you.
 Submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your experience and suitability for the role.

Graduate Structural Engineer | Remedial Consultancy | Pyrmont
Job Summary
Join a growing Sydney engineering consultancy specialising in remedial, structural and façade engineering. An excellent opportunity for a Civil Engineering graduate with an interest in structures to gain practical experience, work alongside experienced engineers and develop their career.
About the Business
Our client is a well-established and growing engineering consultancy based in Pyrmont, specialising in remedial engineering, façade remediation and structural rehabilitation projects.
The business has developed a strong reputation through its technical expertise and long-standing client relationships, working across residential, commercial and government projects.
Their portfolio includes remedial, façade and structural rehabilitation projects ranging from approximately $2 million to $15 million+, providing excellent exposure to different buildings, structural systems and engineering challenges.
With continued growth, they're looking to appoint a Graduate Engineer who can develop alongside their experienced engineering team.
The Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity for a recent Civil Engineering graduate who has a particular interest in structural engineering and wants to develop their technical skills within a consultancy environment.
You'll work closely with experienced engineers, gaining exposure to building inspections, structural investigations, defect assessments, remedial design and construction.
Rather than being limited to office-based design work, you'll have the opportunity to develop an understanding of how buildings perform, why defects occur and how practical engineering solutions are developed and implemented.
The business is looking for someone with a great attitude, strong willingness to learn and genuine ambition to build a long-term career in engineering.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist senior engineers with structural and remedial engineering projects
- Support building inspections, site investigations and defect assessments
- Assist with structural assessments and engineering calculations
- Support the preparation of technical reports and remedial scopes of work
- Assist with structural and remedial design documentation
- Coordinate with engineers, consultants and contractors
- Attend site inspections and develop practical construction knowledge
- Support project delivery and maintain accurate technical documentation
About You
You'll ideally have:
- Completed Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering
- Ideally 1-2 years post graduate experience
- A strong interest in structural engineering, ideally with relevant structural subjects or project experience
- Good understanding of structural engineering fundamentals
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Positive attitude and willingness to learn
- Professional, personable and proactive approach
- Genuine interest in remedial engineering and building structures
Previous internship or work experience within structural engineering, construction or building consultancy would be advantageous but isn't essential.
Recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Attitude, communication and willingness to develop are particularly important.
What's in it for you?
- Join an established and growing engineering consultancy
- Learn directly from experienced structural and remedial engineers
- Exposure to building defects, structural investigations and remedial design
- Opportunity to gain both office-based and practical site experience
- Diverse projects across residential and commercial buildings
- Supportive, collaborative team environment
- Genuine opportunity to develop your technical capability and progress within the business
- Convenient Pyrmont location, close to Sydney CBD
If you're a Civil Engineering graduate with an interest in structural engineering and are looking for an opportunity to learn from experienced engineers and build a long-term career, we'd be keen to hear from you.
Apply via SEEK, email mike@daviesrossconsulting.com.au or contact Michael Forshaw on 0401 724 180 for a confidential discussion.

 - Immediate start on a large, high-profile earthworks project

 How to apply
 Click "Apply" or contact William Gardner at CGC Recruitment on 0435 935 377 or william.gardner@cgcrecruitment.com for a confidential discussion.

bullets: Large pipeline of work, offering excellent career opportunities
Be part of the water infrastructure growth in SEQ
Safety focused culture working within in leading services industry
candidates.content_text:
The opportunity
The Project Engineer delivers projects across capital water infrastructure including valves, hydrants, water pump stations, network renewals, water main replacements and more across the greater and south side of regional Brisbane Area. In addition to managing the Delivery phase of the program's renewals projects, you will be collaborating with design, scheduling, cost and commissioning and maintenance teams to ensure smooth transitions and project success. 
Join us in this fast-paced, stable, and highly rewarding program, where you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of the industry while benefiting from a robust pipeline of long-term, local opportunities.
What you'll do
- Attend planning visits and concept reviews to advise on constructability and delivery across time, cost, safety and quality outcomes
- Support the development of construction methodologies and project schedules for shortlisted design options.
- Develop an understanding of water treatment processes and operational constraints to inform construction planning and methodology.
- Prepare and issue Request for Tender (RFT) documentation based on design drawings and scope of works.
- Support Scheduling, Cost Controls, Community Engagement, Procurement, Estimating, Quality Assurance and Safety teams in developing delivery plans
- Provide technical advice and expertise throughout project delivery phase, promptly addressing any issues and problem-solve to maintain time, cost, quality and safety targets
- Support all procurement activities, including tendering processes and Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) engagements.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, clients, subcontractors and colleagues
What we offer
- Employee benefits including health and wellness initiatives
- Access to Downer Group benefits
- Personalised career development and growth working with an industry leading team.
- Competitive remuneration package
- Safety focused culture working within in leading services industry
- Management support coupled with ongoing training and mentoring
- Career enhancing opportunity to work within an ASX limited company
What we're looking for
- Project delivery experience within the water & or Wastewater Treatment industry (preferred)
- Experience in driving quality outcomes in project delivery
- Degree qualification in civil or mechanical engineering
- Good communication skills
- Good organisational and time management skills
- Ability to build strong relationships with people
- Sound computer skills
'About Energy & Utilities…
Downer's Energy & Utilities business unit is an integrated trans-Tasman team, providing services and solutions that connect communities to essential networks and infrastructure. We design, build, operate and maintain today's critical assets and networks, delivering complete services across the water, electricity, telecommunications, industrial and power generation sectors. Our expertise spans in-house technical smarts, specialist engineering, integrated OEM partners, and dedicated crews of qualified tradespeople.
Downer Group is an employer that acknowledges and embraces the importance of our people's diverse experiences, talents, and cultures. As an inclusive employer, we welcome applications from everyone.
How to apply
Click "Apply" to start your application. We look forward to hearing from you! 
Downer does not accept unsolicited resumes, fees, or costs from recruitment agencies, search firms, or third parties. Candidates are welcome to submit their applications via the advertisement.
candidates.teaser: Join our Energy & Utilities business on a busy program delivering water treatment projects across South/West Brisbane.

Are you ready to turn your degree into something extraordinary?
At Sitzler, you'll have the opportunity to work on some of Australia's most exciting, and complex commercial construction projects while developing the skills, confidence, and experience needed for a successful long-term career in the construction industry.
Our two-year Graduate Program has been designed for recent graduates who are ready to step out of the classroom and into the real world of construction. Through three structured rotations, you'll gain exposure to different aspects of the business, work alongside experienced industry professionals and discover where your strengths and interests lie.
This is not a role where you'll spend your days watching from the sidelines. You'll be involved in real projects, real challenges and real career-building opportunities from day one.
Who We're Looking For
We're seeking graduates who are excited about building a career in construction and ready to gain hands-on experience.
To be eligible, you must:
 - Have completed a relevant degree within the last two years in:
 - Construction Management
 - Engineering (Civil, Structural, Mechanical, etc.)
 - Project Management
 - Estimating or Quantity Surveying
 - Hold Australian Citizenship or Permanent Residency
 - Have a current driver's licence
 - Be willing to work on project sites and travel where required
Skills & Attributes We're Looking For
The successful candidates will demonstrate:
 - A proactive approach and willingness to take ownership of tasks
 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills
 - Effective organisation and time management skills
 - The ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team
 - Adaptability and a positive attitude when faced with new challenges
 - A commitment to delivering high-quality work and continuous improvement
Why Join Sitzler?
You'll work on major construction projects, learn from experienced industry leaders, rotate through different areas of the business, and gain practical experience. Most importantly, you'll be joining a company that is committed to developing the next generation of construction professionals.
Supporting Our People
At Sitzler, we believe in rewarding our people with benefits that support their careers, families, and wellbeing, including:
 - Paid Parental Leave – Supporting employees through important family milestones with paid parental leave entitlements.
 - Employee Referral Program – Earn rewards for helping us attract great people by referring successful candidates to join our team.
 - Company-provided Christmas Shutdown – Enjoy a well-earned break over the festive season with a company-provided week of leave during our annual Christmas shutdown, allowing you to recharge without using your annual leave balance.
Ready to Build Your Future?
If you've graduated within the last two years and are looking for an opportunity that will challenge you, develop you, and set the foundation for an exciting career, we'd love to hear from you!
Applications are now open for Adelaide, Darwin and Perth.
Due to the nature of our projects, preference will be given to Australian Citizens. Applicants who are currently eligible for Australian citizenship or are actively progressing toward citizenship are also encouraged to apply. Please note that some projects may require Australian Citizenship and the ability to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance.
candidates.teaser: Build projects that matter. Build a career that lasts. Join Sitzler for our 2027 Graduate Program.

candidates.abstract: Ready for more than standard floor plans? Work on a wider range of residential projects than you would with most builders.
bullets: Work on a different kind of project almost every week
Have a voice in a close-knit team that values your expertise
Be part of a team that make a real difference to people’s lives.

How many years' experience do you have as a Production Draftsperson?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
candidates.content_text:
Why work with Goldstate Homes
At Goldstate Homes, we build across a wider range of residential markets than most builders: investment homes, knockdown rebuilds, dual occupancies, townhouses, SDA homes, co-living properties, Class 1b rooming houses, dual key homes and turnkey house and land packages. For our team, that means varied and challenging work. No two projects are quite the same, and you'll keep building your skills and experience across many building types. We pride ourselves on speed, service and quality, and we build every home as if it were our own. Our people take real ownership of their work and can see what they've contributed to every home we deliver. If you want to grow your career in a close-knit team that cares about doing things properly, Goldstate Homes is a great place to be.
The role
We're looking for an experienced Production Draftsperson to join the team. Reporting to the Drafting Manager, you'll prepare detailed, accurate working drawings from our current portfolio and custom homes. You'll take each job from sales plans through to construction-ready documentation.
Your day-to-day will include:
- Preparing production and working drawings in Revit.
- Applying client variations, site-specific changes, engineering and developer requirements to drawings
- Checking that plans comply with the NCC, council and regulatory body requirements
- Working with our BDM, Estimating, Contract Admin and Construction teams to provide technical support for client and agent queries
- Liaising with Building Surveyors, Engineers, Councils and Town Planners
- Keeping templates, standards and drawing sets consistent and up to date
About you
- At least 3 years' demonstrated experience as a production draftsperson in volume or custom residential building
- A thorough working knowledge of the NCC and residential construction methods
- Intermediate to advanced Revit skills (essential)
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
- Good problem-solving skills and the ability to find practical solutions
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to manage your workload and meet deadlines
- A team player who does well in a supportive, close-knit environment
What we offer
- Working with a friendly, close-knit team where your contribution is valued
- Varied work across both volume and custom residential projects
- Support and guidance from an experienced Drafting Manager
- Opportunities for professional development and career growth
- Be part of an established and growing residential building company
- A competitive salary

candidates.abstract: Join Council's Emerging Talent Program and gain hands-on experience in water and sewer services while completing a Certificate III qualification.
candidates.location: Bega, Wollongong, Illawarra & South Coast NSW
bullets: Gain a nationally recognised qualification while you work.
Build practical skills across water, sewer and network operations.
Launch your career through Council's Emerging Talent Program.
candidates.content_text:
A career with Bega Valley Shire Council offers the opportunity to engage in meaningful and diverse work that supports the vibrant communities of the south-east corner of NSW. Nestled between rolling hills and some of the state’s most stunning beaches, this region is home to a variety of people who enjoy both rural and coastal living.
As an AR Bluett Award winning Council, we are proud of our dedicated and talented team, whose efforts make our success possible.
With a workforce of over 350, we provide essential services to our communities, including libraries, customer service, finance, children’s services, engineering, project management, road maintenance, water management, environment, parks, gardens, and town centres.
We offer a range of employment benefits to support our staff, which may include:
 - Rostered days off
 - Flexible work arrangements
 - Salary packaging
 - Paid study leave of 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period)
 - Approved study-related expenses
 The Opportunity
We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated individual to join Councils Emerging Talent Program and undertake a Certificate III in Water Industry Operations while gaining practical experience and mentorship across Council's Water and Sewer Services.
As a Water and Sewer Trainee, you will combine vocational studies with hands-on workplace experience across a range of water and sewer network operations functions, including Water Treatment Operations, Sewerage Treatment Operations, Network Maintenance, and Infrastructure Construction. You will gain practical experience in the operation, monitoring and maintenance of essential water and sewer services while developing the skills, knowledge and qualifications required for a rewarding career in the water industry.
The role may also involve travel and participation in residential training blocks associated with your qualification program.
As a participant in Council's Emerging Talent Program, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills through structured learning, on-the-job experience, mentoring and exposure to a broad range of professional disciplines, building a strong foundation for a successful career in local government and beyond.
Council will support your studies by providing paid study leave of 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period) together with approved study-related expenses.
Key responsibilities include:
 - Undertake vocational studies and apply theoretical learning to workplace activities to develop practical skills and knowledge.
 - Assist with the operation, monitoring and maintenance of water and sewerage infrastructure and associated systems.
 - Assist in the construction, installation and repair of water supply and sewerage infrastructure.
 - Assist with the maintenance, servicing and cleaning of water and sewer treatment plant and equipment.
 - Develop skills in inspection, fault finding, testing and problem solving across water and sewer networks.
 This role offers valuable exposure to a broad range of water and sewer operations while developing practical skills and experience to support a future career in Water and Sewer Services.
To view the Position Description, please click here. 
About You
We are seeking two (2) individuals who have obtained a School Certificate (Year 10) or equivalent and hold a NSW Class C drivers' licence (or ability to obtain).
You will have the following skills and experience;
 - Demonstrated analytical and investigative ability to assist in resolving operational problems in the field.
 - Ability to participate in the laying, repair and maintenance of water and sewer mains and associated construction activities.
 - Ability to develop fault-finding and troubleshooting skills relevant to water supply and sewerage systems.
 - Well-developed oral and written communication skills.
 - Demonstrated commitment to learning, teamwork and working safely in an operational environment.
 Benefits
This is a fixed term full-time position working 38 hours per week for a period of two (2) years.
The total remuneration package for this position commences at $29,195.71 to $50,115.52 gross per annum, comprising of:
 - $501.30 to 860.50 per week base salary
 - $60.16 to 860.50 per week superannuation (calculated at 12%)
 Remuneration for this position is dependent upon the age and level of schooling achieved by the successful candidate.
Additional benefits for this position include:
 - Rostered day off scheme (nine day fortnight)
 - Paid study leave of up to 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period)
 - Approved study-related expenses
 - Annual Award salary increases and performance reviews
 - Salary packaging program (SmartSalary)
 - Wellbeing Initiatives – Fitness Passport, Employee Assistance Program, Telus Health App, social club, health monitoring and annual flu vaccinations
 For further information on this position, please contact Luke Cathor - Water and Sewer Networks Operations Coordinator on 0467 787 467.
Applications close 11.59pm AEDT on 22 November 2026.
Applicants must have the right to work in Australia and address the advertised selection criteria demonstrating their suitability for the role.
This position requires applicants to be suitably immunised in line with recommendations from the Australian Immunisation Handbook, mandated Public Health Orders and/or Councils Immunisation Procedure.

candidates.content_text:
Building for Generations through the Pursuit of Excellence
The FKG Construction team has a proud 50+ year history of successfully delivering a variety of commercial construction projects across a wide range of sectors including both government and private clients. We are dedicated to building for generations, achieved through our personable approach with all people, including those within our communities within which we live every day.
We believe our people are the key to our success and we are invested in supporting the wellbeing of our team members, providing skills development opportunities, rewarding performance and recognising high achievement.
As an FKG Group employee you will have access to our range of benefits which includes corporate health insurance discounts, employee assistance program, our “Thrive” wellbeing initiative and many more.
The Role
Keen to kick start your career in the construction industry and work alongside your degree? Then look no further!  Due to recent organisational growth we are looking for our next superstar Cadet!
A cadetship at FKG will give you knowledge across all areas of construction, you'll learn from experienced members of the team, obtain hands-on involvement across a variety of exciting commercial projects and be given excellent learning support and mentorship as you develop your career.
Responsibilities
You will enjoy the variety within your job scope, including:
- Organisation and management of suppliers and subcontractors
- Procurement of trade packages and assistance in developing cost reports;
- Liaison with clients, site staff, design managers, estimators, and project managers
- Estimation, design and contract administration
Experience and Qualifications
 To be considered for this role, you will need:
- To be currently enrolled and successfully completed the first year of your Bachelor of Construction Management/ Urban Development/ Quantity Surveying
- Highly developed organisational, time management and prioritising skills A can-do attitude, self-motivated and willingness to learn;
- An exceptional level of verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills Previous construction industry experience would be an advantage;
- To include your ATAR results on your resume.
Apply Now!
- FKG is an equal opportunity employer, where we recognise the diversity of our team and actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills and potential. We welcome all applications from a wide range of candidates. Selection for roles will be based on individual merit alone. 
- Apply with “Quick Apply” or email hr@fkg.com.au with your CV.

candidates.abstract: Crucial role in the continued success of UGL Regional Linx safely operating and maintaining the Country Regional Network in regional NSW
candidates.location: Bathurst, Blue Mountains & Central West NSW
bullets: Historic piece of regional NSW rail infrastructure
Excellent long term career prospects
Work in a motivated, inclusive, high performing and flexible environment
candidates.content_text:
About UGL Regional Linx
At UGL Regional Linx (UGLRL), we help connect communities across regional New South Wales by managing and maintaining the Country Regional Network (CRN). As a subsidiary of UGL Transport, we are proud to create meaningful employment opportunities in regional and rural communities, with more than 85% of our workforce based across regional NSW.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people feel valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. Guided by our core values, we foster a culture built on collaboration, respect, safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Job Purpose
The Estimator is responsible for preparing project estimates with accurate cost allocations and up to date market knowledge, monitoring the performance of project estimates, managing the change control process associated with project estimates, maintaining the CATS Resource Library with current benchmarked rates, and leading the overall 3MWP estimation process with the support of Infrastructure delivery team subject matter experts, the Procurement team, Finance team, and Assets & Engineering subject matter experts. 
The Estimator supports Project Owners by preparing and updating cost estimates for variations and facilitating the conversion of provisional sums to fixed-cost submissions.
What You'll Be Doing
Be responsible for the estimation of the 3 Year Maintenance Works Program, including the supervision and management of external and internal resources used during the process of estimation
Prepare detailed estimates for every project in the 3MWP in line with the Project Controls Plan process for estimation.
Assist in the preparation of UGLRL Enhancements estimates as required, including the loading of those estimates into CATS
Preparing and updating Estimates for Variations and conversion of Provisional Sum to Fixed Costs submissions
Maintain the UGL Regional Linx CATS Register and Master Resource Library
Maintain up to date Labour, Plant, Material rates within the Master Resource Library
Develop and maintain an “Estimating Manual” for UGLRL Projects. 
Review all project documentation to understand the requirements of the work to include the analysis of technical, contractual and financial requirements.
Explore opportunities for innovation while identifying risk and opportunities.
Maintain accurate and details estimate files.
Maintain awareness of best practice in the industry
Develop innovative estimates and options through knowledge of the latest design and or construction techniques to deliver the best possible outcome for UGLRL
Coordinates and collaborates with subject matter experts on methodology, program, IR, Plant and estimate review processes
Perform trend analysis and actively evaluate project cost and estimate performance
About You
Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Quantity Surveying or similar profession. (Desirable)
3+ years’ experience working in an estimating role
Knowledge of construction, material components, regulations and estimating
Sound knowledge and experience within the rail industry, especially in an O&M context
Ability to read and interpret drawings/plans and specifications
Why Join UGL Regional Linx?
Be part of an organisation that plays a vital role in connecting regional communities.
Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment.
Access opportunities for professional growth and career development.
Contribute to projects with lasting community and infrastructure impact.
Join a business that values diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives.
Diversity & Inclusion
At UGL Regional Linx, we believe diverse teams create better outcomes. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities.
We are particularly committed to increasing female representation across our business and strongly encourage women to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed.
We also encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people living with disability, culturally and linguistically diverse candidates, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and mature-age professionals.
Our recruitment process may include national criminal history checks and pre-employment medical assessments, including drug and alcohol screening.

candidates.content_text:
Get the water flowing on a Defence-linked build in the Top End.
CC Pines is looking for a Site Engineer (Hydraulics) to join our Darwin project full-time, on the ground. We're after someone already based in Darwin, so you can hit the ground running. You'll own the hydraulic scope on site, from setout to commissioning, on a project that'll look very good on your CV.
This is a full-on role. The roster is likely 6 days a week, so we're after someone who wants to be in the thick of it and make things happen. In return, you get real responsibility, a great location and a team that backs you.
About Us
CC Pines is an Australian-owned, family-founded construction company with a 45-year track record of delivering complex, high-risk projects that other contractors won't touch, from embassy builds in Morocco to Defence infrastructure across the Pacific. We work with the Australian Department of Defence, DFAT, and the US Department of Defence, and we've never had a reportable safety incident. We're big enough to run world-class projects, small enough that your voice actually gets heard.
Our values, humble, hungry, smart, aren't a poster on the wall. They're how we pick our people and how we run our sites.
Why Darwin?
This role is based in Darwin, full-time, and honestly, that's one of the best parts of the job.
 - Tax perks that put money back in your pocket. Darwin sits in the Zone A remote area, so you're eligible for the federal Zone Tax Offset. Add no NT land tax for individuals, and a stamp duty concession worth up to $18,600 if you're buying a home in the Territory.
 - A genuine outdoor lifestyle. Mindil Beach sunsets, barra fishing, weekend trips to Litchfield and Kakadu National Parks, and a harbourside city built for getting outside after work.
 - Dry season living. Roughly May to October, you get warm, sunny days and next to no rain.
 - A tight-knit, laid-back community. Small-city feel, big social scene, and a genuine "everyone knows everyone" culture that makes settling in easy.
 - Career runway. Darwin's Defence and infrastructure pipeline is booming, and this puts you right in the middle of it.
Why Join CC Pines?
 - Real ownership of the hydraulic scope on a nationally significant project, not a junior seat in a huge team.
 - Competitive salary plus Territory living benefits.
 - Career progression. We're growing, and we invest in developing our people.
 - A supportive, inclusive team where engineers are trusted and heard.
The Role
As Site Engineer (Hydraulics), you'll be the on-site go-to for all things hydraulic. You'll coordinate subcontractors, check the work against drawings and specs, and keep the program moving, working closely with the Foreman, Site Manager and Project Manager.
What you'll be doing:
 - Managing delivery of hydraulic services on site, including water supply, sanitary drainage, stormwater and fire services
 - Coordinating hydraulic subcontractors and keeping works on program and to spec
 - Reviewing drawings, shop drawings and RFIs, and chasing answers fast
 - Inspecting works, signing off hold points and supporting testing and commissioning
 - Checking installed work against specifications, standards and the NCC
 - Spotting risks early and sorting practical fixes before they hit the program
 - Driving site safety and keeping our zero-incident record intact
 - Keeping progress records, as-builts and reporting up to date for the Site Manager and Project Manager
What We're Looking For
 - Degree in Civil, Mechanical, Hydraulic or a related engineering discipline
 - Site experience delivering hydraulic services on commercial, infrastructure or government projects
 - Working knowledge of AS/NZS 3500, the NCC and fire services requirements
 - Experience coordinating subcontractors and managing quality on site
 - Good eye for detail and strong problem-solving skills
 - Clear communicator who can work with trades, consultants and clients
 - Construction White Card
 - Ideally already based in Darwin, and comfortable with a 6-day-a-week roster
Ready to Get Stuck In?
If you're Darwin based and want a role where you'll own the hydraulic scope and build your career on a standout project, we want to hear from you.

candidates.content_text:
The Organisation
The Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) protects Australia and Australians from threats to their security. ASIO’s people are ordinary Australians but they do extraordinary things – they are our most important asset.
To be successful, we need talented people who are highly capable, dedicated, adaptable and resilient.
We seek to reflect the community we protect. ASIO is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, where all staff are valued and respected. We welcome applications from all eligible candidates, irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious affiliation, age or disability. We are culturally and linguistically diverse, language skills enhance our collective ability to protect Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are encouraged to apply. We are secretive about what we do, not what we value.
At a time when Australia’s security environment is dynamic, diverse and degrading, our work is more important than ever. Join the mission and make a difference every day.
The opportunity
Are you seeking an exceptional career where you can contribute and make a difference to the security of Australia? ASIO’s Technologist Graduate Program is a dynamic and fast-paced 12-month program with intakes in early & mid-2028. The program will set you on a pathway for a career with purpose.
We are seeking university students who have completed their degree before the intake commences, or graduates from the past 3 years who are passionate about technology, continuous learning and working collaboratively to make a difference. On commencement as a technologist graduate, you will be assigned to one of the following streams:
- Science & Engineering
- Data & Analytics
- Information & Cyber Security
- Software Engineering & Development
- IT Platforms
During the 12-month program, you will complete 3 workplace rotations designed to showcase the breadth of work that ASIO undertakes. This work may include:
- Working with industry and domestic partners to investigate, implement and manage new capabilities, networks and technologies.
- Assist in data and AI lifecycle management from acquisition through to sharing and disposal, applying best practice AI and data‑governance frameworks.
- Collaborating with business users to develop high-quality, high-performance software solutions within an agile environment.
- Advancing unique solutions to exploit technically-collected data, including through the use of machine learning and neural networks.
- Reducing the attack surface and assure the ongoing security posture of IT infrastructure.
- Undertaking reverse engineering activities.
- Supporting cyber security investigations.
- Conducting forensic analysis of digital media.
- Providing technical collection capabilities, including telecommunications interceptions.
- Undertaking complex data analysis and innovative visualisation to aid investigations.
- Evaluating technical surveillance counter-measures.
- Engineering high-end mechanical and electrical solutions.
The program will equip you with the skills, experience and knowledge to undertake a wide range of technical roles and to establish a diverse and rewarding career at ASIO.
A merit pool may be created to fill future vacancies which have the same or similar requirements to this position. This merit pool will be valid for up to 18 months.
What you will bring
We are seeking candidates with the following attributes:
- Adaptability
- Curiosity
- Commitment to learning
- Honesty
- Integrity
- Problem solving
- Resilience
- Teamwork
We are seeking candidates with the following capabilities:    
- The ability to work collaboratively
- The capacity to think critically and laterally in solving problems
- The propensity to adapt to emerging issues, events and environments
- Personal qualities that exemplify ASIO’s values and expected behaviours.
Qualifications 
To apply for a graduate program in ASIO, you must have completed a relevant degree prior to program commencement, or no more than 3 years prior.
Candidates are required to have a degree which could include, but are not limited to:
- Cloud Computing
- Data Engineering, Data Science or Data Analytics
- Software or Computer Systems Engineering
- Cyber Security
- Network Engineering
- Computer Science
- Information Technology or Information Systems
- Digital Forensics
- Electrical/Electronic Engineering
- Mathematics or Statistics
- Telecommunications
- Data or AI Management
- Project Management or Business Analysis with an ICT focus.
What we offer you
ASIO provides a number of benefits to its staff including:
- A competitive salary, including a 7.5% allowance for maintaining a TOP SECRET-Privileged Access security clearance.
- Employer superannuation contributions of 15.4%.
- A variety of leave options in addition to the standard 4 weeks annual leave, including stand down between Christmas and New Year.
- Flexible working arrangements. Please note due to our unique working environment, work from home options are not available.
- Study assistance, including financial support and study leave for tertiary education.
- Access to 7 staff-led diversity and inclusion networks.
- Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
- Mentoring opportunities.
Eligibility 
To be eligible to work at ASIO, you must be:
- an Australian citizen
- have completed your degree before the program commences, or graduated in the past 3 years
- assessed as suitable to hold and maintain a TOP SECRET-Privileged Access (TS-PA) security clearance.
Location
Canberra, ACT.
We advertise positions nationally to reach the broadest audience. Please refer to the above location before applying.
Reasonable adjustments
Please let us know if you require any additional assistance or reasonable adjustments during any stage of the recruitment process in order to fully participate in the recruitment process or the workplace. This may include reasonable adjustments to assessment methodologies to enable full participation.
How to apply
ASIO officers’ identities are protected by law. Under section 92 of the ASIO Act, the only declared ASIO officers are the Director-General and Deputy Directors-General. Due to the need to protect our people’s identities, ASIO holds all employment applications in the strictest of confidence. It is essential that you do the same. Please do not discuss your application with others as doing so may adversely affect your potential employment.
Click on ‘Apply online’ to commence your application. Your application must be complete and include the following:
- Succinct responses to the questions below:- Tell us why you are interested in applying for the Technologist Graduate Program.
- Tell us about a technical ‘passion project’ you have been involved in. This can be a personal initiative, tertiary related or other. We want to understand what your technical interests are, what drives you and how you apply it. Feel free to be as technical as you like.
- In our workplace the rate of technical change means there is a premium on knowledge sharing. How important is learning and communicating to you?
- A current CV, no more than 2 pages in length, outlining your employment history, the dates and a brief description of your role, as well as any academic qualifications or relevant training you may have undertaken.
- A copy of your academic transcript. If you have not yet graduated, please provide your most up-to-date transcript. This can be an unofficial copy as long as it is issued by your tertiary provider.
- Details of 2 referees, which must include a current or previous supervisor. ASIO will not contact your referees without advising you prior to doing so.
Read the ASIO People Capability Framework and Core Capability Guide, available on ASIO’s website. Ensure your responses address the relevant capabilities and levels outlined in these frameworks.
Use of artificial intelligence in recruitment processes
ASIO does not use any form of artificial intelligence (AI) at any point in the recruitment process.
All applications are reviewed by a selection panel. We recognise some applicants may use AI technologies to draft applications or prepare for interviews. If you wish to use AI, we recommend doing this only for initial drafts and ensure that your application is personalised and accurately reflects your skills, experience and qualifications.
Additionally, be aware of the privacy policies of any AI tool you use. Be mindful of the information you are entering into AI tools (personal details, work history, etc) and how using it may link you to potential ASIO employment, noting that you are expected to be discrete and maintain confidentiality with your application.
If you are invited to attend interview, the use of AI tools and recording devices during interview is strictly prohibited. Should AI tools or recording services be detected, your application, and any future applications may be discontinued.
The recruitment selection process – timeframes
Our selection process is rigorous and extensive. All employment decisions and selection processes at ASIO are based on merit principles and candidates must be prepared to undergo various selection stages. The stages may include application assessment, eligibility checks, online testing, skills-based assessment and interview.
We ask all applicants for their patience throughout the process.
As we are recruiting for the early & mid-2028 Technologist Graduate Program intakes, candidates can expect the following timeframes for the recruitment selection process:
- - Program advertised October and closes Monday 30 November 
- Assessment centres will likely run in March 2027. 
Employment conditions
Employment is under the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979. Conditions of service are similar to those applying in the Australian Public Service. We recognise entitlements accrued under the Public Service Act 1999 and provide for continuation of superannuation under the Commonwealth schemes. Salary packaging arrangements are also available.
Australian Workplace Equality Index
ASIO has achieved the Australian Workplace Equality Index (AWEI) Gold Standard in 2024, 2025 and 2026, recognising ASIO’s inclusion work and positive culture. ASIO was the first Australian intelligence agency to achieve this status.
For more information about ASIO, please visit: www.asio.gov.au.

candidates.content_text:
Company description:
STERIS is a leading provider of infection prevention and procedural products and services, focused primarily on the critical markets of healthcare, pharmaceutical and research and medical devices. Our mission is to help our Customers create a healthier and safer world by providing innovative healthcare and life science product and service solutions around the globe. We have 12,000 employees worldwide, with over 3,000 in Customer-facing sales and service roles. Founded as Innovative Medical Technologies in Ohio in 1985, the company was renamed STERIS in 1987. Many of the businesses that have been acquired and integrated into STERIS have much longer operating histories, notably the American Sterilizer Company founded in 1894. The STERIS Vision is inspired by our Customers' efforts to create a healthier and safer world, and guided by our legacy of leadership and innovation; we strive to be a Great Company. To STERIS, this means we will make a difference by providing world-class product and service solutions for our Customers, safe and rewarding work for our People, and superior returns for our Shareholders.
Job description:
Position Summary
As a Project Engineer, you will play a key role in delivering exceptional customer outcomes through the design, coordination, and end-to-end execution of capital medical equipment projects across the STERIS Healthcare portfolio throughout Australia and New Zealand. From initial project scoping and design development through to installation, commissioning, and project completion, you will ensure projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in compliance with clinical and regulatory requirements.
Working collaboratively with Sales, Project Managers, Installation Teams, Clinical Stakeholders, Consultants, Contractors, and Vendors, you will provide technical expertise, design guidance, and project coordination across multiple healthcare facilities and technologies. This role is ideal for a proactive engineering professional who thrives in a customer-focused environment and is passionate about delivering high-quality healthcare solutions while upholding STERIS's commitment to safety, quality, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence.
What You Will Do
 * Define project scope, objectives, milestones, and deliverables aligned with customer and business requirements.
 * Provide design, planning, and coordination of CSD, Endo and Surgical projects from pre-sales through to installation and project closeout.
 * Develop equipment layouts, specifications, CAD & REVIT drawings, sizing reports, schedules, budgets, quotations, and technical proposals.
 * Review project requirements, drawings, and specifications to ensure compliance with healthcare standards and best practices.
 * Develop and maintain project plans, tracking scope, schedule, cost, quality, and resource requirements.
 * Provide technical expertise during customer presentations, design workshops, and tender submissions.
 * Coordinate customers, consultants, contractors, vendors, and internal stakeholders to ensure successful project delivery.
 * Prepare and manage project budgets, quotations, and tender responses within approved financial targets.
 * Monitor project progress, quality, and safety performance in accordance with STERIS standards and quality management systems
 * Identify, assess, and manage project risks, issues, and change controls throughout the project lifecycle.
 * Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including architects, builders, consultants, and clinical teams.
 * Support continuous improvement initiatives and contribute to LEAN, 5S, Sustainability, and One Team One Goal objectives.
 * Provide National Installation Coordinator coverage during periods of leave.
 * Promote and uphold STERIS values, culture, safety, quality, and customer satisfaction in all activities.
The Experience, Skills and Abilities Needed
Required:
 * Bachelor's Degree in Engineering.
 * Proficient in CAD and/or REVIT drafting packages.
 * Good understanding of CSD Standards e.g. AS 5369:2023.
 * Demonstrated experience delivering complex projects, preferably within healthcare, medical devices, capital equipment, engineering, construction, or technical environments.
 * Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel as required.
Preferred:
 * Project Management experience.
 * Experience working with healthcare facility projects, sterilisation departments, operating theatres, or medical capital equipment installations.
 * Knowledge of quality management systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Others:
 * Strong project planning and organisational skills.
 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 * Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building capability.
 * Commercial awareness and budget management skills.
 * Ability to assess and mitigate project risks.
 * Customer-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering exceptional service.
 * High attention to detail and quality standards.
 * Ability to remain calm under pressure and make sound decisions
